_comment: REAL-WORLD DRIVER RECORDS. Read drivers.py before editing this file.
EVERY NUMBER IS AS OF THE FIRST RACE OF THAT SEASON — what the driver
brought with him, not his career total. Prost has 28 wins in 1988 and 51
by the end of his career; only the 28 is true on the grid at Silverstone.
That tense is what makes these facts safe to say in round one and still
safe to say in the finale, whatever the user does to the championship.
titles         world championships won BEFORE this season. 0, never null.
champion_years the years of those titles. Length must equal `titles`, and
every year must be earlier than the season — the test
enforces both, because a wrong year dates a title wrong on
air and that is the exact failure this file exists to avoid.
wins           Grand Prix wins BEFORE this season. 0, never null.
rookie         true only for a genuine first full season.
contender      is he expected to fight for THIS year's title? An editorial
judgement, and the gate on the 'chasing an eighth' lines —
without it Alonso is asked about a third title from an
Aston Martin in 2025.
new_team       he arrives at this team for this season.
note           ONE hand-written clause, used verbatim, no terminal stop.
Anything true of exactly one man lives here rather than in
a schema nobody could keep correct.
note_void_on   what STOPS the note being true: 'win', 'podium' or
'start'. Hulkenberg's record for starts without a podium
ends at his first podium; Arnoux's 'last win was five
seasons ago' ends at his next win. A note without this is
a fact about the past that your season cannot reach —
'the youngest race winner this sport has ever had' stays
true however the championship goes. WHEN YOU ADD A NOTE,
ask what would falsify it before you leave this out.
alias          other spellings the mods use. Accents, spacing and Jr./Sr.
are already handled by folding — only add what folding
cannot reach ('Bortoletto' for Bortoleto).
SCOPE IS THREE SEASONS. Adding a fourth is adding a block here and
nothing else. Do not add a season you are not prepared to check.
TEAMS. Each season block also carries a `teams` map: what the CAR is like
this year. `strength` and `weakness` are clauses used verbatim, in the
present tense, and describe the machinery rather than the results — the
booth is calling a race the user is driving and must not appear to know
how the real season went. Every team named here must be a `team` value on
at least one driver, or nothing can ever reach it; drivertest.py checks.
`quotes` - signature radio lines, per OCCASION. Occasions are 'win',
'pole', 'podium', 'good', 'bad', 'incident'.
A catchphrase in the wrong mouth, or on the wrong occasion, is worse than
no catchphrase: it turns a character into a parrot. So each is tied to one
driver AND one kind of moment, judged from his own race arc, fired rarely
and at most once per driver per session.
These appear as RADIO CARDS and are never spoken - rival audio was removed
because edge-tts has no accents for a full grid. Written to be read.
The 1988 set is deliberately thin and deliberately NOT presented as
verbatim: team radio barely existed then and the surviving quotes are from
interviews. Those entries are what a driver would plausibly say on the
radio, not a claim about something he said.

win: That is what I came here for.

bad: This car does not want to turn.

good: I've got more in this. Much more.
bad: Something is broken. I can feel it.

Gerhard Berger.note: who won the last two races of last season for Ferrari

Riccardo Patrese.note: the most experienced man on this grid by some distance

Satoru Nakajima.note: the first Japanese driver to hold a full-time Formula One seat

Rene Arnoux.name: René Arnoux
Rene Arnoux.note: whose last win came five seasons ago

Stefan Johansson.note: a man with plenty of podiums and still no win

Stefano Modena.note: with a single Grand Prix start to his name so far

McLaren.strength: the Honda turbo, and a chassis low enough to make the most of it
McLaren.note: the strongest package on this grid, and the two quickest drivers in it

Ferrari.strength: a turbo V6 that gives away very little in a straight line
Ferrari.weakness: a car that has never been as easy to drive as the McLaren

Williams.weakness: a naturally aspirated Judd V8, after losing the Honda engines over the winter
Williams.note: a team that has gone from the best engine on the grid to a customer V8

Lotus.strength: the same Honda turbo the McLarens are running
Lotus.weakness: a chassis that has never made proper use of the Honda engine

Benetton.strength: the best of the naturally aspirated cars, with the Cosworth V8
Benetton.note: the team betting hardest on turbos being banned

March.strength: one of the neatest chassis in the pit lane, narrow and light on drag

Arrows.strength: a Megatron turbo, which is a BMW four-cylinder under another name

Tyrrell.weakness: a customer Cosworth and not much budget behind it

Ligier.weakness: a car nobody at the team has been able to make work

Minardi.weakness: a small budget and a long way to go

Rial.weakness: a single car and very little behind it

Zakspeed.weakness: a turbo of their own building that is well off the pace

Larrousse.weakness: a Lola chassis and a customer engine at the back of the grid

AGS.weakness: one of the smallest operations in the paddock

EuroBrun.weakness: the problems of a brand-new team, all at once

Coloni.weakness: a single car and pre-qualifying to survive before any of it counts

Osella.weakness: an old turbo and a chassis that has seen several seasons

Scuderia Italia.weakness: a first season in Formula One, with a Dallara chassis

Lewis Hamilton.note: with more race wins than anyone in the sport's history

Max Verstappen.note: the youngest race winner this sport has ever had

good: That's more like it. Simply lovely.

Sergio Perez.name: Sergio Pérez
Sergio Perez.note: who took his first Grand Prix win at the end of last season

Fernando Alonso.note: back on the grid after two seasons away

bad: I don't want to talk about it now.
I'm not happy with this. Not at all.

Kimi Raikkonen.name: Kimi Räikkönen
Kimi Raikkonen.note: with more Grand Prix starts than anyone in the history of the sport

bad: Leave me alone, I know what I'm doing.
incident: Leave me alone, I know what I'm doing.

Mick Schumacher.note: the reigning Formula 2 champion, and a Schumacher back on the grid

Mercedes.strength: straight-line speed, and the best power unit on the grid
Mercedes.weakness: a car built to run flat to the ground, in the season the floor rules punished exactly that

Red Bull.strength: high-speed corners, and a car that rotates beautifully on the way in
Red Bull.weakness: a very narrow setup window, and a difficult car to drive outside it

McLaren.strength: a Mercedes power unit and a car that is kind to its tyres

Ferrari.strength: a much stronger engine than the one they had last season
Ferrari.weakness: straight-line speed that is still not where it needs to be

Alpine.strength: a car that comes alive on a hot track and a rough surface

AlphaTauri.strength: much of the same aerodynamic thinking as the Red Bull, in a friendlier car

Aston Martin.weakness: a car built to run flat to the ground, and new floor rules that took away what made it work

Alfa Romeo.weakness: a customer Ferrari at the back of the midfield

Williams.weakness: the smallest budget on the grid, and a car to match
Williams.note: a team rebuilding under new ownership

Haas.weakness: a car that will not be developed at all this year, with everything going into the next one
Haas.note: two rookies and a machine nobody is going to improve

good: That's more like it. Simply lovely.

Lewis Hamilton.note: in red for the first time in his career

bad: This is not possible. Not again.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli.note: eighteen years old, and he has Hamilton's old seat

Fernando Alonso.note: the oldest man on this grid, and still here

bad: I don't want to talk about it now.

Nico Hulkenberg.name: Nico Hülkenberg
Nico Hulkenberg.note: with more Grand Prix starts than any driver in history without a podium

Gabriel Bortoleto.note: Formula 3 champion and then Formula 2 champion, back to back

Franco Colapinto.note: who came up from the reserve seat to take the second Alpine

McLaren.strength: the best car in the pit lane, and the kindest of all of them to its tyres

Ferrari.strength: a strong race car, and the driver line-up everyone is talking about

Red Bull.strength: enormous performance once the window is found
Red Bull.weakness: a car that is very hard to drive when it is not

Mercedes.strength: a much better-behaved car than the ones that came before it

Williams.strength: a genuine step forward, and an experienced driver to make use of it

Racing Bulls.strength: a quick car on its day, in the hands of two very young drivers

Aston Martin.weakness: a car that has not moved forward, with everything aimed at next season

Alpine.weakness: a difficult car and a difficult season in front of them

Haas.strength: a completely reworked car after last year's problems

Sauber.weakness: a car that belongs at the back of the grid, and a long wait for a works future
